events.title: Hormuz · severely constrained
events.fact: Flow: 7.6 million bbl/day; 13.1 below pre-war, per IEA.
events.meaning: Inference: lost export access can shut production in even when underground resources and installed capacity remain intact.
events.watch: Sustained delivered cargoes, not an announcement of reopening.

events.title: Saudi bypass · shutdown reported
events.period: Early September 2026; confirmed in 18 Sep report
events.fact: IEA reported the East–West pipeline shut after attacks. Reopening by 30 September is not verified here.
events.meaning: Inference: a bypass is only useful if the pipeline, loading port and onward sea lane all work.
events.watch: Verified restart and actual Yanbu departures.

events.title: Yanbu + Fujairah · relief, then retreat
events.fact: Combined exports: 4.1 → 7.8 → 5.5 million bbl/day.
events.meaning: Inference: replacement routing softened the loss but did not fully replace the blocked flow.
events.watch: Both endpoints and onward-route reliability.

events.title: Gulf of Oman · transfer bottleneck
events.fact: Kpler: STS handling 7.2 million bbl/day versus 0.16 in 2025. Repeated transfers can count the same cargo more than once.
events.meaning: Inference: more transfer activity need not mean more unique supply; support services and vessel time can become the constraint.
events.watch: Unique cargo deliveries, waiting time and repeated handling.

events.title: United States · added supply
events.fact: Output gain: 520 thousand bbl/day, per IEA.
events.meaning: Inference: useful replacement supply, subject to crude quality and transport constraints.
events.watch: Production versus export and delivered volumes.

events.title: Brazil · added supply
events.fact: Output gain: 470 thousand bbl/day, per IEA.
events.meaning: Inference: additional Atlantic supply increases alternatives for importers.
events.watch: Sustained output and refinery compatibility.

events.title: Kazakhstan · added supply
events.fact: Output gain: 440 thousand bbl/day, per IEA.
events.meaning: Inference: production gains still require functioning export access.
events.watch: Export-terminal availability.

events.title: Venezuela · added supply
events.fact: Output gain: 300 thousand bbl/day, per IEA.
events.meaning: Inference: replacement volume is not an identical crude-grade substitute.
events.watch: Delivered volumes and buyer eligibility.

events.title: Canada · expanded Pacific outlet
events.fact: Trans Mountain nominal capacity: 890 thousand bbl/day. Expansion in service since May 2024.
events.meaning: Inference: another export outlet diversifies market access. Capacity is a ceiling, not observed throughput or new production.
events.watch: Actual utilization, tanker departures and planned additions versus completed additions.

events.title: Nigeria · refining shifts trade
events.period: Company report 25 May 2026; April demand share
events.fact: Dangote cites 650 thousand bbl/day capacity and nearly 80% of domestic petrol demand served in April.
events.meaning: Inference: local refining can reduce product imports while consuming crude that could otherwise be exported. Company-reported results need corroboration.
events.watch: Actual runs, domestic deliveries, exports and feedstock availability.

events.title: Grangemouth · refinery became import terminal
events.fact: Petroineos confirms the site now imports and distributes fuels.
events.meaning: Inference: regional fuel demand survives the refinery closure; the supply chain shifts toward finished-product imports and terminal logistics.
events.watch: Product arrivals and replacement supply, rather than local crude intake.

events.title: California · idled fuel-making assets
events.period: Benicia fully idled April 2026; Los Angeles status checked 30 Sep
events.fact: Valero confirms Benicia processing units idled. Phillips 66 says its Los Angeles refinery is idled.
events.meaning: Inference: a national crude surplus does not guarantee local gasoline availability. Imports, fuel specifications and terminal capacity matter.
events.watch: Delivered replacement fuel and remaining refinery outages.

events.title: Russia · shadow shipping persists
events.fact: KSE estimates 5.3 million bbl/day total seaborne crude + products; 150 of 268 active tankers classified as shadow fleet. The 56% figure counts ships, not barrels.
events.meaning: Inference: sanctions can change routes, costs and buyers without stopping all physical movement. KSE classification is not a court finding for each cargo.
events.watch: Volume shares, destination uncertainty, insurance and enforcement changes.

events.title: Iran · named vessels, continuing cargoes
events.fact: Treasury identified BREEZE V and CRYSTAL as carrying millions of barrels of Iranian oil to China in 2026.
events.meaning: Inference: physical flow and legal access are separate questions. These are government allegations and dated designations, not live vessel tracking.
events.watch: Cargo arrivals and jurisdiction-specific designations or licences.

events.title: Malaysia · transfers obscure origin
events.period: Alleged May 2025 shipment; Treasury action 24 Apr 2026
events.fact: Treasury says LYNN received Iranian crude through an offshore transfer and delivered it to China.
events.meaning: Inference: loading location can differ from crude origin. STS transfers alone do not establish sanctions evasion; they also serve routine logistics.
events.watch: Chain of custody, stated origin and corroborated delivery records.

events.title: China · large buyer, opaque destinations
events.fact: KSE assigns 37% to China, 22% to India and 33% to unknown destinations.
events.meaning: Inference: unknown destinations are a material gap. Do not assign every unreported cargo to China or assume it is undelivered.
events.watch: Revisions when cargoes discharge.

events.title: India · alternative transfer hub has costs
events.fact: Kpler discusses West Coast India as an alternative STS location, with weather and support-service constraints.
events.meaning: Inference: a longer shuttle ties up ships and may raise freight without increasing final demand.
events.watch: Realized transfers versus proposed logistics scenarios.

events.title: Asian import cuts · not just efficiency
events.fact: IEA reported combined China/Japan crude imports down nearly 6 million bbl/day from pre-conflict levels.
events.meaning: Inference: reduced refinery feed can ease crude competition while worsening product scarcity. Lower imports are not automatically lower end-use needs.
events.watch: Refinery runs, demand, product stocks and rationing separately.

events.title: Diesel · the product bottleneck
events.fact: IEA: Gulf + Russian net diesel/gasoil exports fell 1.6 million bbl/day. Atlantic refining margins reached records.
events.meaning: Inference: extra crude alone cannot replace unavailable diesel-making capacity or the missing product shipment.
events.watch: Product cracks, refinery runs and distillate inventories.

events.title: Cape route · more oil tied up in travel
events.fact: EIA compares Arabian Sea–Netherlands sailing at 19 days via Suez with 34 around Africa.
events.meaning: Inference: rerouting can increase oil aboard ships at unchanged daily demand. The extra travel inventory is not an extra barrel produced.
events.watch: Voyage length, congestion, laden ships and arrival timing.

events.title: A lower run rate can be routine maintenance
events.period: Structural US seasonality; not a current outage claim
events.fact: Planned refinery turnarounds are periodic maintenance; EIA describes first-quarter and autumn concentration in the US.
events.meaning: Inference: classify a decline only after checking seasonality, outage duration and announced restart. A low reading alone is not proof of closure.
events.watch: Prior same-month range and verified operator notices.

chokes.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokes.note: Gulf export outlet; pipeline bypasses provide only partial alternatives.

chokes.name: Strait of Malacca
chokes.note: Indian–Pacific connection. Lower traffic can reflect upstream supply loss, not closure of Malacca. Table 2 used consistently; source Table 3 differs for 2025 Q4.

chokes.name: Suez + SUMED
chokes.note: Combined canal and pipeline series; not tanker transits alone.

chokes.name: Bab el-Mandeb
chokes.note: Quarterly history predates the September attacks. Do not treat the Q2 increase as current safe passage.

chokes.name: Danish Straits
chokes.note: Baltic gateway. Excludes Kiel Canal; location marker represents Great Belt.

chokes.name: Turkish Straits
chokes.note: Black Sea access; traffic, weather and transit management can alter timing.

chokes.name: Panama Canal
chokes.note: Canal dimensions and water availability constrain eligible vessel movements; not every tanker can use it.

chokes.name: Cape of Good Hope
chokes.note: Alternative long route around Africa, rather than a narrow strait.

water.note: All oil on water. In-transit draw: crude −117 mb; products −64 mb. Floating build offset part of that draw. Floating = idling more than 12 days in this source.
